what_happened: The design job "Design early per-job PRs and dropping the local staging branch" was rejected at the final verdict. The verifier raised two major findings and no blockers. (1) Soundness: the note says the verifier runs against the same commit the producer ended on, and that rebuilds happen only on a send-back or a moved main. But the landing gate requires the landing commit to add the verifier's closing records, so a commit built when the producer ends cannot be the landing commit (section 2 items 1-4, section 7). (2) Evidence: the note says the 7.0-minute prediction fits the CI overlap mechanism, but the measured stage figures show the overlap can save at most about 3.7 minutes (section 5). The event lists no unmet acceptance criteria and no failed checks.
cause: Design jobs have no required step that checks a note's mechanism and headline numbers against the existing landing gate code and the measured stage data before the note builds on them. The note was written from the request's framing and not from the real landing flow, so it missed that the gate requires the verifier's closing records in the landing commit. It also took a predicted saving at face value when the measured stage figures cap it at about 3.7 minutes. Criteria check that sections and predictions exist, not that the sequence of commits is possible or that the arithmetic fits the data. Only the verifier reads the code and records, at the end. This repeats the same weakness as the neighbouring landing-design jobs.
prevention: Add a required survey-and-check step to every design job before the producer writes. (a) Trace the proposed flow step by step against the code that enforces it, here the landing gate's rule about which commit may land and what records it must add. Write the order of commits and what each stage sees. (b) Recompute every predicted saving from the recorded stage durations and state the upper bound the data allows. Where a cited note or record disagrees with the prediction, the note must say so. The reading lists these as criteria with a demonstration each: the commit sequence cites the gate code, and each number cites its record. Where a prior attempt rejected on a similar premise, its findings are carried into the reading.
proposed_request: Revise the design note docs/design/early-pr-no-staging-branch.md for early per-job pull requests and dropping the local staging branch. Outcome: the note describes a flow that the landing gate can accept, and its predicted saving matches measured data. Acceptance: (1) Before writing, read the landing gate code and list what the landing commit must contain, including the verifier's closing records. Section 2 then gives the exact order of commits: what is built at producer end, what the verifier adds, what is pushed, and what CI sees. It states which commit lands and when a rebuild or force-push is needed, and removes the claim that the verifier runs against the same commit that lands. (2) Section 7 on force-push after a rebuilt commit is consistent with that order. (3) Section 5 recomputes the saving from the recorded stage durations, states that the CI overlap can save at most about 3.7 minutes, and either lowers the 7.0-minute prediction or names the other mechanism that would account for the rest, with its record. Each figure cites its source. (4) The measurement method that would score the prediction is stated. (5) Add a CHANGELOG.md entry. Only the design note and CHANGELOG.md may change.
